text:
Nina: dropped a new compact-row experiment called "scale-lock + sampling presets" in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/unique (frame: compact-scale-lock). Looking for quick takes on: (1) the idea of locking sparkline y-scale per-row vs global, (2) how to show sampling preset shortcuts in compact mode, (3) whether to normalize heatmap buckets across rows or per-row, and (4) copy for the sampling preset tooltip.

Omar: quick skim 50d I think lock-per-row helps surface regressions but makes cross-row comparisons harder. users who care about trend shape want per-row; product managers doing comparisons want global. suggest a toggle: "Scale: per-row / global" and remember user preference per-console.

Lena: bucket normalization: strongly prefer global buckets by default. per-row normalization hides platform-wide spikes. we can add a small legend indicator "normalized" when per-row mode is on.

Maya: sampling presets in compact mode need to be ultra-compact. proposal: show a single icon (scatter icon) next to the panel title; clicking opens a tiny menu with presets (Low / Medium / High) and keyboard shortcuts (L/M/H). show tooltip: "Sampling preset: Low = fast, coarser; High = slower, more accurate." Keep copy < 70 chars.

Nina: good. what about showing an ephemeral toast when user changes preset that says "Sampling set to High (approx +/- 4% p95 variance)"? need to be careful with numbers. maybe keep approximate phrasing.

Omar: accessibility: presets menu should be a menubutton with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. shortcuts announced via aria-describedby. also include aria-live polite when sampling completes: "Sampling complete: results may differ slightly from real traffic".

Lena: UX nuance: when switching between global and per-row scale, animate the bars slightly (crossfade heights) so users don't misinterpret instant changes as new data. respect reduce-motion.

Maya: copy micro-nit: preset names Low/Med/High are concise but vague. alternatives: Economy / Balanced / Accuracy. Which reads better to non-technical folks?

Nina: prefer Economy/Balanced/Accuracy. they map better to cost/accuracy tradeoffs in the tooltip.

Omar: also suggest showing sample size in the toast: "High (n≈1.2k)" so users have immediate context. round numbers for readability.

Lena: heatmap bucket strategy: implement global fixed buckets (configurable). allow user override per-panel: settings -> Buckets: fixed (default) / per-row. show a small hint icon in the legend when non-default chosen.

Maya: tiny CSS for compact preset icon + focus ring:
```
.panel-header .preset-icon { width: 18px; height: 18px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; }
.panel-header .preset-icon:focus { outline: 2px solid #06b6d4; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; }
```

DesignerBot: accessibility scan:
- Contrast: preset icon on primary header color passes 4.5:1 at 18px.
- Motion: recommended crossfade <180ms and no transform when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
- Screen reader: suggested aria-label for menubutton: "Sampling presets, current: Balanced". For the scale toggle use: "Scale mode, current: global".

Nina: one more UX edge-case 4a1 if the user enables per-row scale and then pans time window, the p95 values can jump wildly. propose a banner on first toggle: "Per-row scale is on: values compare relative trends, not absolute latency" with a "dont show again" link.

Omar: telemetry ask: record events for preset changes, scale-mode toggles, and whether users use keyboard shortcuts L/M/H. will help tune defaults.

Lena: decision proposal summarised:
1) Default: global heatmap buckets + global sparkline y-scale.
2) Add a toggle: Scale = Global / Per-row (remember preference). animate transitions with crossfade <180ms and respect reduce-motion.
3) Presets icon in header opens compact menu: Economy / Balanced / Accuracy with keyboard shortcuts L/M/H. toast on change shows rounded sample size (n≈).
4) Allow per-panel bucket override in settings (fixed buckets by default). show legend hint when overridden.
5) ARIA: menubutton + aria-live polite messages for sampling updates; label toggles for screen readers.

Maya: +1 to all. I'll update the Figma frames: compact-scale-lock-v2 and add the preset menu + scale toggle. I'll also write the short tooltip copy: "Economy = faster, coarser samples; Accuracy = slower, finer samples." (64 chars). Will tag y'all when pushed.

DesignerBot: accessibility follow-up: ensure the toast uses role=status (not alert) to avoid interrupting screen-reader users. Also include aria-atomic=true so the full message is read.

Nina: perfect. thanks everyone 680
